title: Cycling the Danube from source to sea
instructions: You are going to listen to a radio interview with a young woman who cycled the whole length of the river Danube. Answer questions 1–9 in no more than FOUR words. You will hear the recording twice. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Egy rádióinterjút hallasz egy fiatal nővel, aki végigbiciklizett a Duna teljes hosszán. Válaszolj az 1–9. kérdésre legfeljebb NÉGY szóval. A felvételt kétszer hallod; a 0. a példa.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Welcome back to Open Road, the programme for people who'd rather take the long way round. My guest today is Isla Fraser, who this summer cycled the entire length of the river Danube, from its source in the Black Forest in Germany all the way to the Black Sea. Isla, welcome.

script.speaker: I
script.text: Thanks, Owen. It's lovely to be here – and to be sitting on something that isn't a bike saddle, to be honest.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Let's start at the beginning. What made you want to do it?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Well, I'm a primary school teacher, so I get long summer holidays, and I'd been doing short cycling trips in Scotland for years. But I wanted something bigger – something that would take me through lots of different countries without ever having to get on a plane. And the Danube's perfect for that. It flows through ten countries, and there's a signposted cycle route for most of the way.

script.speaker: P
script.text: And how long did it take you in the end?

script.speaker: I
script.text: I'd planned on six weeks, but it ended up being seven and a half. Partly because of the weather, and partly because I kept stopping in places I liked. I spent four days in Vienna when I'd only meant to spend one.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Did you have any problems with the bike itself?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Only one serious one, and that was in Austria, of all places – the easiest part of the whole route. I hit a pothole near Linz and bent the back wheel so badly that it wouldn't turn any more. Luckily, there was a bike shop in the next village, and the owner replaced the whole wheel that same afternoon.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Where did you sleep? Hotels?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Very rarely – that would have cost a fortune. I had a small tent, and most nights I stayed at campsites, which along the Danube are generally cheap and pretty good. In the bigger cities I stayed with hosts from a website for touring cyclists, where people offer you a bed and a shower for free.

script.speaker: P
script.text: You went through Hungary, of course. What do you remember about it?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Oh, lots! Budapest was stunning, obviously, and I went to one of the thermal baths, which was exactly what my legs needed. But my favourite memory is from a village further south, near Baja. I'd stopped at a little shop to buy some water, and an old man sitting outside asked me, mostly with gestures, where I was going. When I said 'the Black Sea', he burst out laughing and insisted that I join his family for dinner. They'd made a huge pot of fish soup – bright red, really spicy, full of paprika – and I think I had three bowls.

script.speaker: P
script.text: And did things get harder the further east you went?

script.speaker: I
script.text: In some ways, yes. Serbia in July was incredibly hot – it was forty degrees on some days – so I started setting off at about five in the morning and stopping by lunchtime. Cycling in the afternoon just wasn't an option. Then in Romania and Bulgaria the main challenge was dogs. There are a lot of farm dogs that run out into the road and chase you, and the first time it happened I was genuinely scared. A Dutch cyclist I'd met in Belgrade had given me some advice: carry a whistle, and blow it as hard as you can when a dog comes towards you. It sounds silly, but it worked almost every time.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Which part of the river was the most beautiful?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Without a doubt, the Iron Gates. That's the gorge where the Danube forms the border between Serbia and Romania. The river suddenly gets much narrower, and the cliffs go straight up on both sides. People had told me it was spectacular, but photos really don't do it justice. I sat there for an hour just watching the boats go by.

script.speaker: P
script.text: And when you finally reached the Black Sea?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Honestly? At first it was a bit of an anticlimax. The cycle route ends in a fairly ordinary port town, and it was pouring with rain. I'd imagined this big emotional moment on a beach, and instead I was standing in a car park, soaking wet. But then I took my shoes off, walked straight into the sea in the rain, and just started laughing. That was my big moment in the end.

script.speaker: P
script.text: So what's next?

script.speaker: I
script.text: Everyone keeps telling me I should do the Mississippi next, but I'm not ready to cross the Atlantic with a bike just yet. Next summer I'm going to cycle along the Rhine, from Switzerland to the North Sea. It's a lot shorter, so my legs might actually forgive me.

script.speaker: P
script.text: Isla Fraser, thank you very much, and good luck with the Rhine.

example.prompt: What does Isla do for a living?
example.explanation: A helyes válasz: primary school teacher (általános iskolai tanító). Isla elmondja, hogy tanítóként hosszú nyári szünete van, ezért tudott ilyen hosszú útra menni.

items.prompt: How many weeks did the whole journey take?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: seven and a half (hét és fél hét). Csapda: Isla hat hétre tervezte az utat („I'd planned on six weeks”), de végül hét és fél hét lett belőle – a kérdés a tényleges időtartamra vonatkozik.
items.evidence: I'd planned on six weeks, but it ended up being seven and a half.

items.prompt: Which part of the bike had to be replaced?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: the back wheel (a hátsó kerék). Linz közelében egy kátyú miatt annyira elgörbült a hátsó kerék, hogy nem forgott, ezért a szerelő az egész kereket kicserélte („replaced the whole wheel”).
items.evidence: bent the back wheel so badly that it wouldn't turn any more

items.prompt: Where did Isla stay on most nights?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: at campsites (kempingekben, sátorban). Csapda: szállodában csak nagyon ritkán aludt, a nagyvárosokban pedig kerékpáros vendéglátóknál – de a legtöbb éjszakát („most nights”) a sátrával kempingekben töltötte.
items.evidence: I had a small tent, and most nights I stayed at campsites

items.prompt: What did the family near Baja serve Isla for dinner?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: fish soup (halászlé). Az idős férfi családja egy nagy fazék csípős, paprikás, élénkpiros halászlét főzött, és Isla három tányérral evett belőle. A termálfürdő Budapesthez tartozik, nem a vacsorához.
items.evidence: They'd made a huge pot of fish soup

items.prompt: Why did Isla stop cycling by lunchtime in Serbia?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: because of the heat (a hőség miatt). Szerbiában júliusban hihetetlenül meleg volt, néha 40 fok, ezért hajnali ötkor indult, és délre befejezte a napot – délután nem lehetett tekerni.
items.evidence: Serbia in July was incredibly hot – it was forty degrees on some days

items.prompt: What did Isla use to deal with the farm dogs?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: a whistle (síp). Egy holland kerékpáros azt tanácsolta neki Belgrádban, hogy vigyen magával sípot, és fújja meg teljes erőből, ha egy kutya közeledik – ez szinte mindig bevált.
items.evidence: carry a whistle, and blow it as hard as you can when a dog comes towards you

items.prompt: Which part of the river did Isla find the most beautiful?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: the Iron Gates (a Vaskapu). Ez az a szoros, ahol a Duna Szerbia és Románia határát alkotja; a folyó hirtelen összeszűkül, a sziklák függőlegesen emelkednek – Isla szerint ez volt kétségkívül a legszebb szakasz.
items.evidence: Without a doubt, the Iron Gates.

items.prompt: What was Isla's first impression of arriving at the end of the route?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: an anticlimax / disappointing (kiábrándító, csalódás). Isla szerint a megérkezés eleinte „a bit of an anticlimax” volt: egy hétköznapi kikötővárosban, szakadó esőben egy parkolóban állt a várt érzelmes tengerparti pillanat helyett. A nevetés és a „nagy pillanat” csak később jött, amikor besétált a tengerbe.
items.evidence: At first it was a bit of an anticlimax.

items.prompt: Which river is Isla planning to cycle along next?
items.explanation: A helyes válasz: the Rhine (a Rajna). Csapda: sokan a Mississippit javasolják neki, de ő még nem áll készen arra, hogy biciklivel átkeljen az Atlanti-óceánon – jövő nyáron Svájctól az Északi-tengerig a Rajna mentén teker.
items.evidence: Next summer I'm going to cycle along the Rhine
